candidates.name: LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
verified_facts: The point cloud is an archive of highly accurate 3D x,y,z points and component attributes.
EA time-stamped DSM and DTM raster products are derived from point-cloud data.
Historic archiving means a matching point cloud may not exist for every surface-model tile.
Point returns are classified into ground and surface-object classes during processing.
semantic_limits: Point-cloud availability/classification is supporting lineage and cannot replace the canonical DTM raster sample.

candidates.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: Time-stamped DTM is available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m depending on the survey.
GeoTIFF tiles are aligned to the OS Grid, use metres and are referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
EA states vertical accuracy of +/-15cm RMSE.
The metadata index gives survey date, resolution, transformation and geoidal model by location.
semantic_limits: Time-stamped lineage must be matched through metadata; publication availability alone does not identify the composite contributing survey.

candidates.name: LIDAR DSM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: Time-stamped DSM includes vehicles, buildings, vegetation and terrain.
GeoTIFF tiles are aligned to the OS Grid and referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
EA states vertical accuracy of +/-15cm RMSE.
Metadata index catalogues provide survey date, resolution, transformation and geoidal model.
semantic_limits: DSM is excluded from the primary bare-earth height-difference result.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Surface Model (DSM) - 1m
verified_facts: The 1m DSM covers about 99% of England and includes surface objects.
The 2022 composite merges time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Repeat-survey selection uses newest, best-resolution data and bilinear interpolation where resampling occurs.
Metadata index catalogues identify the contributing survey by location.
semantic_limits: A 1m DSM is still a surface-object model and cannot replace the 1m bare-earth DTM.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite First Return DSM (FZ_DSM) - 1m
verified_facts: The 1m first-return DSM includes objects above terrain where the first return is not ground.
It is derived from National LIDAR Programme capture from 2016 to 2022.
Survey overlaps are merged using feathering.
Metadata index catalogues identify the survey used at a location.
semantic_limits: First-return and feathered surface data are diagnostic only and excluded from primary DTM extrema.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 GML feature types
verified_facts: ContourLine, SpotHeight and LandWaterBoundary are distinct feature types.
Spot-height propertyValue is a height above Newlyn or another British height datum.
Feature and geometry identifiers are regenerated when a tile is refreshed.
GML geometry uses EPSG:27700.
semantic_limits: Vector feature lifecycle and identifiers are not a parcel-level raster observation.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 contour data
verified_facts: Contour tiles include per-tile metadata such as flying-date information.
Spot heights are selected by an automated process from closed contours.
Spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places.
Genuine depressions can produce spot heights lower than surrounding contours.
semantic_limits: Automated rounded spot heights are secondary vector evidence and not primary parcel extrema.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 vector tiles
verified_facts: Contour layers are supplied as a national MBTiles vector-tile set.
The vector-tile representation uses Web Mercator EPSG:3857.
Feature attributes are exposed only at configured zoom levels.
semantic_limits: Web Mercator vector-tile portrayal is excluded from native EPSG:27700 numeric terrain sampling.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 downloads and XML schemas
verified_facts: OS publishes XML schema resources for contour products, gridded products and viewing-style metadata.
semantic_limits: Schema validation establishes encoding structure only; it does not certify elevation accuracy or survey lineage.

candidates.name: Land and Terrain Portfolio
verified_facts: The portfolio distinguishes OS Terrain 5 and OS Terrain 50 from land-use/site products.
OS Terrain 5 is the more detailed terrain family while Terrain 50 is a lower-resolution open terrain product.
semantic_limits: Portfolio routing is product-family evidence, not parcel-specific terrain measurement.

candidates.name: WCS 2.0 XML/POST Protocol Binding Extension
verified_facts: The approved extension carries WCS requests with HTTP POST and XML encoding.
It defines request structures for GetCapabilities, DescribeCoverage and GetCoverage.
Protocol binding is separate from WCS processing extensions.
semantic_limits: Transport/encoding choice does not change source elevation accuracy, interpolation or survey lineage.

candidates.name: WCS 2.0 KVP Protocol Binding Extension
verified_facts: The approved extension carries WCS requests via HTTP GET key/value-pair encoding.
Its conformance target is WCS protocol communication rather than coverage-value semantics.
semantic_limits: KVP transport does not prove native resolution, native CRS, interpolation state or data authority.

candidates.name: CIS ReferenceableGridCoverage Extension
verified_facts: The extension provides instantiable structures for referenceable-grid coverages within the OGC coverage model.
Referenceable-grid structure is distinct from a rectified regular grid.
semantic_limits: Coverage grid structure must be established explicitly; conformance alone does not validate EA raster values.
